anya: FYI I'm seeing a 15-30% p95 increase on qwen-70b after last night's kernel-router change. Spikes happen on requests with long prefixes (>1024). Rolling back the router reduces p95 back to baseline. cc @mike @lee

mike: same here, p99 spikes on 3 nodes in us-west-2. attaching a tiny profiler snapshot:
```
-- perf sample (node-3) --
kernel_router: kernel_v2 (fallbacks=4)
kv_cache: hits=87% evict_rate=0.12
latencies: p50=18ms p95=74ms p99=154ms
batch_size: median=2 mean=2.1
rope_scale_factor: 1.22
```

perf-bot: Perf alert: routing_change -> kernel_v2 applied 2026-03-17T02:12:07Z (change-id: rtr-4123) :warning:

lee: quick notes from log-level debug: kv cache entries look correct but we see repeated small evictions that coincide with prefix re-syncs. hypothesis: RoPE table generation differs between kernel_v2 and kernel_v1; scaling mismatch leads to KV mismatched addresses and extra cache churn. qwen-70b uses rotary base ~10000 in our loader vs 8192 used in some kernels.

sana: can we force a safe fallback in config? propose runtime.kv_precision_override=fp16 + runtime.kernel_policy=prefer-v1 for qwen-70b until we finish. That prevents fp8 path for kv and keeps kernel v1 routing.

anya: repro steps I used locally (quick):
```bash
# repro (short)
./run_inference --model qwen-70b --prefix-file long_prompt.txt --tokens 1500 --kernel-policy kernel_v2 --kv-precision fp8
# profiler attached: /tmp/prof-1955.tar.gz
```

mike: deployed a canary rollback in us-west-2 (nodes 2-4) to kernel_v1, watching tail. If p95 drops in 10m we can rollback cluster wide.

deploy-bot: rollout started: revert-router-to-v1 by mike. Rollout id: rb-8903. 0->20% currently.

lee: also noticed batcher heuristics are producing tiny batches for these long-prefix calls (median=2). Small batches + fp8-kv warming seems to amplify the penalty. Might tweak batcher.min_batch_delay for qwen traffic class.

anya: agreed. short-term plan: 1) rollback kernel-router 2) force fp16 kv for qwen 3) increase min_batch_delay for qwen-class on canary 4) add unit test to catch RoPE table mismatch across kernels.

mike: +1. i'll keep the rollback until tomorrow morning US. if stable we'll do a controlled reintroduce with an A/B that forces rope-table sanity checks.

perf-bot: Note: creating perf-regression issue perf/1955 (auto) and linked traces.

anya: thanks team — keeping this thread as primary triage. will post results and the repro artifact link after full rollback verified. :thumbsup:
